## New Investigation Idea

- **[2026-10-20] The most AI-specific piece Burry has written this autumn, "The AI Cloud Oligopoly, Stages of Grief & a Flashing Bear Market Indicator" (Short Thoughts, about 10-10), is not in the wiki. The 10-19 ingest pulled in the follow-up that depends on it, and AI & Tech, the domain its title is about, has seen neither.** [[finance/investor-letters/source-burry-foundations-bear-market-caldera-2026-10-17]] opens by pointing readers back to it, and the raw file's text keeps returning to it ("Last week I called this stage of the market 'denial'"). It is not in `raw/finance/` and no wiki page has the title. Its arguments have already moved real money in the wiki. Burry's 10-11 post folds his MU/NVDA/NBIS shorts into SMH and NDX puts ([[finance/investor-letters/source-burry-trading-post-2026-10-11]]), and the 10-19 paper-trader run sold AMAT's last third partly because "Burry's SMH puts now cover AMAT". On the AI & Tech side, [[ai-tech/data-hyperscaler-ai-revenue-2026-06-27]] and [[ai-tech/model-ai-ecosystem-constraint-edges-2026-06-27]] treat the hyperscalers as a growing market. Neither tests the "oligopoly" framing: that AI cloud is consolidating into a few firms whose returns may not cover their capex. AI & Tech hasn't been updated since 10-10, so the Burry bear case keeps growing in Finance without being checked against AI & Tech's own revenue numbers. Concrete step: clip the Short Thoughts piece from Substack into Clippings so the sorter files it. Then add a 'Bear view' line to the hyperscaler revenue page that sets Burry's claim against its own AI-revenue/capex ratio. The 2026-09-15 Kakashii oversupply idea is still open and is a natural partner.

## New Cross-Domain Connection

- **[2026-10-20] Fred's live Prosus position is filed in the AI risk table as "Non-US value / SOTP — no signal". But Prosus is mostly a Tencent stake, and AI & Tech's China page ranks Tencent Cloud as China's #3 AI cloud, running on Huawei Ascend chips and export-controlled NVIDIA H20s. Burry's 10-11 post adds a test the holding has never been given: he owns Tencent but refuses Alibaba until it stops issuing shares to pay for AI.** [[finance/trading-portfolio]] holds 30 PRX at €41.07 (−12.6%, on Watch after a mechanical Exit on 10-02 and a patience override). Its AI-risk row (line ~325) sees only a NAV-discount story. [[ai-tech/data-china-ai-cloud-silicon-2026-06-27]] puts Tencent Cloud at 15% share (~$9B) on a mixed Ascend + H20 fleet. That ties Tencent's AI build-out to two things the PRX thesis never mentions: US export-control decisions and Huawei's chip roadmap. The same page's "Investment signal" table lists only BABA for Western investors. It misses that Fred already has China AI-cloud exposure through Prosus. [[finance/investor-letters/source-burry-trading-post-2026-10-11]] sharpens the point. Burry holds Tencent, JD and Meituan but won't rebuy Alibaba until it is in the HK$70s "or reverses its AI-funding share issuance". In June he had bought BABA partly for its "active buyback" ([[finance/investor-letters/source-burry-trading-post-2026-06-12]]). The line he draws is how a company pays for AI capex, from cash flow and buybacks or by diluting shareholders. That is his US circular-financing critique moved to China. The 10-17 Foundations piece also argues that in a 2000-style top the already-broken stocks rise while the leaders fall, which fits a −12.6% NAV-discount holding as a long. Concrete step for the next PRX reassessment: check Tencent's last two quarters for AI capex against free cash flow and whether the buyback continues. If Tencent passes Burry's test, write that into the Patience Override justification. If it is diluting like Alibaba, the "thesis intact" claim no longer holds.

## New Investigation Ideas

- **[2026-10-19] The 10-18 briefing's new pending idea, CF Industries, is the seventh "Magic Formula rank + chart trigger" recommendation. The first six went 0 for 6. CF is also a nitrogen maker whose cheap P/E may be a Hormuz supply shock, not a value signal. Nobody has checked which before it gets approved.** The briefing card (fred-dashboard `morning-briefing.md`, `briefing-rec-CF-US-2026-10-18`) says enter on a close above $123.50 (SMA50 reclaim), stop $115.25, €1,000, on MF#22, P/E 8.6, EY 16.1%, ROIC 24.5%. That is the same recipe [[finance/models/model-portfolio-management]]'s 10-11 review found in all six recommended-trades closes (FOUR, BBY ×2, AF, MEGP, MONY): a Magic-Formula-ranked name plus a technical confirmation, 0 wins, exited in about two weeks. Two things make CF riskier than those six. First, it is a textbook Lynch cyclical. [[books/book-lynch-one-up-on-wall-street]] section 8 says a cyclical's P/E is lowest at the earnings peak, and 10-05 already flagged the same trap for Micron. Second, Gulf producers ship a large share of the world's seaborne urea and ammonia through the Strait of Hormuz. A closed or contested strait raises nitrogen prices and CF's margins, and a reopening cuts them. The paper book has traded Hormuz at least six times, always as an oil story (XOM, COP, OXY), and [[finance/investor-letters/source-dalio-strait-of-hormuz]] never mentions fertiliser. [[finance/investor-letters/source-grantham-resource-thesis]] lists fertiliser as a "potential future screen", but its case is long-run phosphate scarcity (Morocco), not gas-based nitrogen. CF would be the wiki's first fertiliser position, entering on the wrong half of Grantham's thesis. Concrete step, before approving: (1) pull CF's 10-year EPS and compare trailing EPS with the 10-year median (above roughly 1.5× means the 8.6 P/E is on peak earnings); (2) note the current Hormuz status and the urea/ammonia price trend in the trade thesis, so a reopening is a named exit trigger; (3) put the card's Key Risk on record before CF reports Q3 in early November.
